a.d: The subject initiates and directly carries out the action toward an object.
ex: 동생이 바람이 불기 전에 창문을 **닫았어요**. — My sibling closed the window before the wind blew.

b.d: The subject undergoes the action or experiences a state caused by an external force or agent.
ex: 거센 바람에 열려 있던 창문이 저절로 **닫혔어요**. — In the strong wind, the open window closed by itself.

im-c56-01.tip: In Korean, when describing natural occurrences, environmental changes, or accidental events, using passive verbs (-이/히/리/기-) sounds much more natural and objective than active verbs.

im-c56-01.q: Fix the sentence where an active verb was mistakenly used to describe an external sound being perceived.
answers: 창밖에서 시원한 빗소리가 작게 들렸어요.
창밖에서 시원한 빗소리가 작게 들렸어요
창밖에서 시원한 빗소리가 작게 들립니다.
창밖에서 시원한 빗소리가 작게 들립니다
im-c56-01.hint: Sound reaching ears naturally is expressed using passive 들리다: 들렸어요.
im-c56-01.why: The sound reaches ears as a sensory perception, so the passive verb 들리다 must be used instead of active 듣다.

items.ex: 안개가 걷히자 저 멀리 산이 보였다.

im-c56-01.say: 바람이 세게 불어서 열려 있던 창문이 쾅 하고 닫혔어요
answers: 바람이 세게 불어서 열려 있던 창문이 쾅 하고 닫혔어요
바람이 세게 불어서 열려 있던 창문이 쾅 하고 닫혔어요.
im-c56-01.hint: Because the wind blew hard, the open window slammed shut.

im-c56-01.q: Write a sentence describing that a window closed by itself in the wind, using 창문이 and 닫혔어요.
im-c56-01.sample: 바람이 불어와 열려 있던 창문이 저절로 닫혔어요.
im-c56-01.why: Using passive verb 닫히다 to describe an object closing naturally due to wind.

base.en: The door closed in the wind.

steps.en: In the strong wind, the window closed by itself.
In the strong wind that suddenly blew, the open window closed with a sound.

ko: 아침에 일어나 창문을 여니 저 멀리 눈 덮인 산이 한눈에 보였다.
방 안으로 시원한 아침 바람이 들어오고 새소리도 맑게 들렸다.
갑자기 세찬 바람이 불어와 열려 있던 방문이 쾅 하고 닫혔다.
en: When I woke up in the morning and opened the window, the snow-covered mountain far away was visible at a glance.
A cool morning breeze came into the room and birdsongs were heard clearly.
Suddenly a fierce wind blew and the open room door slammed shut.

im-c56-01.q: What passive verbs describe sensory experiences in the passage?
options: 보였다 (visible) and 들렸다 (audible)
먹었다 and 마셨다
달렸다 and 뛰었다
im-c56-01.why: 보이다 (to be seen) and 들리다 (to be heard) express passive sensory perceptions.

im-c56-01.q: Why did the room door close in the story?
options: Because a sudden fierce wind blew into the room
Because a guest intentionally locked it with a key
Because an automated machine malfunctioned
im-c56-01.why: The text states that a sudden fierce wind blew, causing the door to shut.

items: I can recognize and conjugate single-word passive verbs with suffixes -이/히/리/기-.
I can describe natural sights, sounds, and physical events objectively in passive voice.

a.d: Used with transitive base verbs lacking a suffixal passive form to describe resulting states.
ex: 새로운 규칙이 드디어 **만들어졌어요**. — A new rule has finally been established.

b.d: Unnecessary and grammatically flawed stacking of -아/어지다 onto verbs already containing -이/히/리/기-.

im-c56-02.tip: Never add -아/어지다 to verbs that already have passive suffixes: say 닫히다 (not 닫혀지다), 열리다 (not 열려지다), and 잊히다 (not 잊혀지다).

im-c56-02.q: Correct the double passive error in the sentence describing a door opening.
im-c56-02.wrong: 자동문 센서가 켜지면서 문이 스르륵 열려졌어요.
answers: 자동문 센서가 켜지면서 문이 스르륵 열렸어요.
자동문 센서가 켜지면서 문이 스르륵 열렸어요
자동문 센서가 켜지면서 문이 스르륵 열립니다.
자동문 센서가 켜지면서 문이 스르륵 열립니다
im-c56-02.hint: Use the correct single passive form 열리다: 열렸어요.
im-c56-02.why: 열리다 is already passive; adding -어지다 creates an incorrect double passive (열려지다).

im-c56-02.say: 다음 달 학술 대회 발표 일정이 최종적으로 정해졌어요
answers: 다음 달 학술 대회 발표 일정이 최종적으로 정해졌어요
다음 달 학술 대회 발표 일정이 최종적으로 정해졌어요.
im-c56-02.hint: The presentation schedule for next month’s conference was finally decided.

im-c56-02.q: Write a sentence stating that a new club guideline was created, using 규정이 and 만들어졌어요.
im-c56-02.sample: 회원들의 의견을 모아 동아리의 새로운 규정이 만들어졌어요.
im-c56-02.why: Expressing the establishment of a rule with the passive form 만들어지다.

steps.en: The club’s new rule was created with everyone’s consent.

tokens: 오랜 토론 끝에 동아리의 새로운 규정이
steps.en: After long discussion, the club’s new rule was officially made with members’ active approval.

ko: 이 전통 도자기는 천 년 전 장인들의 뛰어난 솜씨로 만들어졌다.
세월이 흘러 표면의 무늬는 조금 지워졌지만 여전히 아름답다.
박물관에 안전하게 보관되어 많은 사람들에게 소중한 기억으로 그려진다.
en: This traditional ceramic was made with the superb craftsmanship of artisans a thousand years ago.
Although patterns on the surface were slightly erased as time passed, it is still beautiful.
It is safely preserved in the museum and pictured as a precious memory by many people.

im-c56-02.q: How was the traditional ceramic created according to the passage?
options: By the superb craftsmanship of artisans a thousand years ago
By an automated modern machine last month
Imported from a foreign department store yesterday
im-c56-02.why: The first line states it was made by artisans a thousand years ago (장인들의 뛰어난 솜씨로 만들어졌다).

im-c56-02.q: Which verb in the passage expresses fading or being erased over time?
options: 지워졌다 (was erased / faded)
만들어졌다 (was made)
보관되었다 (was preserved)
im-c56-02.why: 지워지다 means to be erased or rubbed off over time.

items: I can form resultant passive expressions using -아/어지다 on verbs.
I can identify and eliminate double-passive mistakes like 닫혀지다 or 잊혀지다.

im-c56-03.h: 자신의 의지 (-기로 하다) vs 환경의 변화 (-게 되다)

a.d: Emphasizes that the subject made a conscious personal choice or plan.
ex: 제가 직접 지원해서 서울 본사로 **가기로 했어요**. — I decided to go to Seoul headquarters through my own application.

b.d: Expresses that outcomes developed naturally due to external circumstances, rules, or fate.
ex: 회사 인사 발령으로 서울 본사에서 **일하게 되었어요**. — Due to personnel transfer, I came to work at Seoul headquarters.

im-c56-03.tip: -게 되다 is also used to deliver personal achievements with modesty, politely attributing success to good fortune or teamwork rather than boasting.

im-c56-03.q: Fix the sentence where an outcome caused by company appointment is awkwardly phrased as a boastful command.
im-c56-03.wrong: 회사 방침에 따라 제가 새 팀장을 맡도록 하세요.
answers: 회사 방침에 따라 제가 새 팀장을 맡게 되었습니다.
회사 방침에 따라 제가 새 팀장을 맡게 되었습니다
회사 방침에 따라 제가 새 팀장을 맡게 됐어요.
회사 방침에 따라 제가 새 팀장을 맡게 됐어요
im-c56-03.hint: Use the polite, modest passive result ending -게 되었습니다: 맡게 되었습니다.
im-c56-03.why: Announcing an appointment resulting from company policy requires the modest outcome marker -게 되다.

items.ex: 우연한 계기로 한국 문화를 접하게 되었다.

im-c56-03.say: 회사 인사 발령으로 다음 달부터 부산 지사에서 근무하게 되었습니다
answers: 회사 인사 발령으로 다음 달부터 부산 지사에서 근무하게 되었습니다
회사 인사 발령으로 다음 달부터 부산 지사에서 근무하게 되었습니다.
im-c56-03.hint: Due to company personnel appointment, I have come to work at the Busan branch from next month.

im-c56-03.q: Write a sentence explaining that you came to know a good film through a friend’s recommendation, using 소개로 and 알게 되었어요.
im-c56-03.sample: 친한 친구의 소개로 그 훌륭한 영화를 알게 되었어요.
im-c56-03.why: Using -게 되다 to describe getting to know something through external circumstances.

base.en: I came to work in Korea.

steps.en: Due to company transfer, I came to work at the Korea headquarters.

tokens: 해외 지사 근무를 마치고 회사 발령으로 인해
steps.en: Finishing overseas branch service and due to company transfer, I came to work with new teammates at the Korea headquarters in Seoul.

ko: 처음에는 한국어에 서툴렀지만 좋은 친구들을 만나 한국 문화를 깊이 이해하게 되었다.
회사 인사 발령으로 올해부터는 서울 본사 기획팀에서 근무하게 되었다.
새로운 환경에서 책임감 있는 프로젝트를 맡게 되어 기대가 크다.
en: At first I was clumsy in Korean, but meeting good friends I came to understand Korean culture deeply.
Due to company personnel transfer, from this year I have come to work in the planning team at Seoul headquarters.
Coming to take charge of a responsible project in a new environment, my expectations are high.

im-c56-03.q: Why did the author come to work in the Seoul planning team?
options: Due to regular company personnel transfer
Because the author won an international lottery
Because all other branch offices closed down permanently
im-c56-03.why: The author states: 회사 인사 발령으로 올해부터는 서울 본사 기획팀에서 근무하게 되었다.

im-c56-03.q: What stylistic nuance does -게 되다 add to the passage?
options: It politely expresses outcomes shaped by circumstances or destiny with modesty
It expresses angry frustration against superiors
It demands immediate obedience from readers
im-c56-03.why: -게 되다 explains changes brought about by external situations in a polite, humble tone.

items: I can express circumstantial developments and life milestones with -게 되다.
I can announce new positions, assignments, and fortunate coincidences with modest etiquette.

im-c56-04.h: 직설적 능동 비난 vs 완곡한 피동 배려

a.d: Can sound accusatory or blunt by placing direct agency onto the conversation partner.
ex: 네 목소리가 안 들려. 크게 말해. — I cannot hear your voice. Speak louder.

b.d: Attributes issues to the phone line, equipment, or environment, saving face for both speakers.
ex: 지하철이라 그런지 목소리가 잘 **안 들려요**. — Perhaps because it is the subway, your voice is not heard well.

im-c56-04.tip: In business and polite daily Korean, rephrasing awkward situations in passive voice softens potential blame and maintains harmonious etiquette.

im-c56-04.q: Fix the blunt, accusatory telephone phrase to a courteous passive expression.
im-c56-04.wrong: 당신이 조용히 말해서 내가 소리를 안 들어요.
answers: 주변 소음 때문에 목소리가 잘 안 들려요.
주변 소음 때문에 목소리가 잘 안 들려요
주변 소음 때문에 목소리가 잘 안 들립니다.
주변 소음 때문에 목소리가 잘 안 들립니다
im-c56-04.hint: Use passive 들리다: 목소리가 잘 안 들려요.
im-c56-04.why: Saying 목소리가 잘 안 들려요 politely shifts the issue to the audio environment without blaming the caller.

items.ex: 임원 회의가 다음 주 화요일로 연기되었다.

im-c56-04.say: 지하철 터널 안이라서 그런지 통화가 자꾸 끊기네요
answers: 지하철 터널 안이라서 그런지 통화가 자꾸 끊기네요
지하철 터널 안이라서 그런지 통화가 자꾸 끊기네요.
im-c56-04.hint: Maybe because we are inside the subway tunnel, the phone call keeps cutting off.
im-c56-04.why: Passive 끊기다 with soft conversational ending: 끊기네요.

im-c56-04.q: Write a polite business notice stating that the meeting was postponed to next week, using 회의가 and 연기되었습니다.
im-c56-04.sample: 부서 내부 사정으로 오늘 회의가 다음 주로 연기되었습니다.
im-c56-04.why: Using the formal passive 연기되었습니다 for professional announcements.

base.en: Your voice is not heard well.

steps.en: Because surroundings are noisy, your voice over the phone is not heard well.
Because surroundings are noisy with subway rumble, the speaker’s voice over the phone is not heard clearly.

ko: 갑작스러운 기상 악화로 인해 오늘 오후 출발 예정이던 모든 항공편이 결항되었습니다.
승객 여러분께 불편을 드려 대단히 죄송하며, 대체 항공편 예약이 신속히 진행되고 있습니다.
자세한 탑승 안내는 안내 데스크를 통해 공지될 예정입니다.
en: Due to sudden worsening weather, all flights scheduled to depart this afternoon have been canceled.
We deeply apologize to passengers for the inconvenience, and alternative flight bookings are proceeding swiftly.
Detailed boarding notices will be announced via the information desk.

im-c56-04.q: What happened to this afternoon’s flights?
options: All flights were canceled due to worsening weather
Flights took off two hours earlier than scheduled
All passengers were transferred to trains automatically
im-c56-04.why: The notice begins: 갑작스러운 기상 악화로 인해 모든 항공편이 결항되었습니다.

im-c56-04.q: Why are passive expressions like 결항되었습니다 and 공지될 예정입니다 preferred in official public announcements?
options: They state factual realities objectively without placing personal blame on individuals
They hide who the airline manager is
They sound playful and casual
im-c56-04.why: Passive voice in official announcements establishes objective, formal, and respectful communication.

items: I can communicate softly in phone calls and meetings by replacing accusatory active verbs with passive verbs.
I can comprehend formal passive announcements in public transport and business settings.
